## SmallPen operation rules

Use the supplied CLI path, otherwise `smallpen` on PATH. The installed CLI's help/schema governs available fields and flags, even when its version matches this Skill; source examples can differ from the installed build. Discover operations with `help`, then `help OBJECT`, `help OBJECT ACTION`, and the returned schema queries. Read only the action and input fields needed now; use returned IDs, not invented selectors. Put write JSON in files. Honor the user's authoring tool choice; read-only App inspection does not authorize App edits.

Start with one target and compact text for navigation, then use the installed CLI's supported outputs. Three design outputs have distinct roles: **specification** (`view --as spec` / `export --format spec`) supplies implementation constraints, native geometry, Token/component sources, instance overrides and diagnostics; **wireframe** shows spatial structure on an approximate character grid; **PNG** shows high-fidelity appearance for visual acceptance. Implement from constraints such as `height=hug`, not the resulting pixel height alone. Compare `layout.hash`, revision and selection across outputs. `export --format png --evidence` produces all three and JSON evidence from one native solve. `--element` expands selected-node details. Unknown geometry stays `?`/`partial` with a reason; never infer actual coordinates from seed bounds, bindings from equal values, or business rules from appearance. Coverage proves only the listed combinations. Search large result files instead of loading all JSON: `resultFile.text.path` contains readable specifications. Preserve LF/spaces and display wireframes in monospace without soft wrapping. A text-only caller may export PNG but must not claim visual inspection.

Supply a stable batch ID before retryable edits, reuse it only with identical input, and read the write receipt. Follow scoped error recovery and current schemas. An explicit reverse edit is a new guarded write; it is not history rollback. Read check issues, skipped coverage and rendering limits before describing a result as verified.

These are tool rules. The scene below defines how to use the tool for this task.

## CLI rules from source

- CLI version: 0.1.0-alpha.12. Use the installed CLI's help/schema when its version differs.
- Replies are compact JSON with a 8 KiB budget. Large complete results use resultFile paths; --full expands data, while --stdout explicitly requests large stdout.
- Temporary results have unique names in one system temporary directory. Each invocation cleans managed files older than 30 minutes. Read them promptly; --output keeps requested deliverables.
- When the project uses Tokens: No --theme: use each project's group defaults, never the App's active selection. Libraries without stored defaults use the real Default option, else the first option in library order.
- Project defaults < explicitly requested Scenario themes < explicit --theme. Override only named groups; unspecified groups keep defaults. Presentation chooses structure and does not implicitly choose a theme.
- Groups and options are project-defined. Platform, language, light/dark, brand and density are examples, never required dimensions or fixed flags. --locale changes CLI labels only.
- token theme default --theme Group/Option explicitly saves a project default; the App's own active selection changes only in the App (or with a set-active-token-themes operation through advanced apply). View, validate and export never save a selection.
- Scoped checks: Validate canonical data and report text/layout/contrast issues and coverage; a page checks every version and a component every variant unless one is named.

# Application design

Deliver an editable SmallPen package, its design system, requested prototype connections and scoped review results. Application implementation belongs to the later development task.

## Understand the project

On first use, establish what software the user wants, who uses it, the core tasks and content, the expected platforms, and which platform to deliver first. Ask about missing choices that affect scope, structure or behavior. Use answers already supplied; a complete brief can proceed without another approval round. Bundle related questions. Keep the user's language unless the project requires another one.

Inspect an existing package and the project's design conventions before adding definitions. Maintain one `DESIGN.md` alongside the package, updating it rather than creating a file each round. Record confirmed requirements, the first platform, capabilities each platform must preserve, style direction, shared definitions, justified structural differences and review targets/combinations. Treat user choices about page reuse, theme control and authoring tools as acceptance requirements. Mark assumptions and sample data. Missing key requirements require questions; ordinary visual details can be chosen and recorded.

## Tokens, components, then pages

Work by name. Use `token` for values, `token theme` for groups/options/defaults, `component define` for shared components, `page draw` for business pages and `flow` for prototype links. Use `page set` or `component set` for scoped field edits. Name the platform or variant when needed; do not transfer flags from one command to another. Theme options use `Group/Option`, as in `token theme add --theme Viewport/Tablet`. Write `{token.path}` to bind a Token. UI text can use `string` Tokens bound to `text`; `boolean` Tokens bound to `visible` control visibility.

Use the CLI's supported layout to place UI elements. Keep task-specific geometry literal where it is a design rule, such as a logo. The CLI maintains the native component catalog and system views; do not draw duplicate component showcase Pages. Keep business pages on one canvas unless the user asks for another or the modules are clearly separate. Links and prototype flows work only within one canvas; an element inside a copy links by `Page / Copy / Element`.

The bundled font covers Latin only. For Chinese or another script, import a font with `asset font import` and bind its family through a Token. Give sibling elements and each kind of project object distinct names. A rename onto a used name is numbered; `view --as issues` reports duplicates and `Name [2]` selects a duplicate for repair.

Read existing theme groups, raw Token definitions and components. Define the needed shared vocabulary before drawing pages: typography, colors, spacing, radii, borders and useful reusable dimensions. Groups are project-defined; do not require a platform, language or light/dark group. Add a platform group only if this project's value differences need it. Create or reuse Tokens, then bind them when creating components and nodes. Check actual bindings; an inventory of unused Tokens is not a design system. Do not leave binding work for the developer.

Default to content-driven height. Height Tokens describe intentional shared constraints, such as a control size, touch target or editor viewport. Text, list, card, section and page heights follow content, line height, padding and gaps; use supported hug/content sizing for them. Do not generate a height Token per node, page, path or sample string, or rename those measurements into a large set of "semantic" sizes. Stored measured bounds can serve as preview geometry without becoming Tokens. If a renderer cannot compute content height, report that gap and verify the supported renderer; do not hide it by binding every measured height. CLI Token-match advice is a heuristic, not a requirement to bind each suggested dimension. Remove obsolete content-height bindings before deleting their Tokens, and check that widths, wrapping and required content still work.

Check both the Token's type and its binding target. `stroke` and stroke-width bindings require a stroke on the bound node; `strokes.N` and `fills.N` require that indexed paint to exist. When converting a FRAME into an INSTANCE, do not carry bindings for paint the instance no longer owns. Keep shared paint bindings in the component, or use a supported override on the intended descendant. A successful write or CLI PNG does not prove that the App can resolve the binding before expanding instances.

Build shared navigation, headers, inputs, actions and business-content components, then compose their instances on pages. Express component states, sizes and suitable structural alternatives as variants of one component. Labels such as Save and Cancel use instance text overrides rather than separate component definitions. Compose standard shell parts and content instances in a page frame. The current instance API does not expose an arbitrary content slot; do not insert business children under an instance and assume they replace its source subtree.

Review reusable components before propagating them. Cover applicable default, hover, focus, selected, disabled, loading and error states. Check standalone components, nested instances and actual page overrides; a focus outline can fit the source component yet fail after its parent resizes. Use representative long names, paths, multiline descriptions and action combinations. Give title, secondary text, source, status and actions distinct roles and enough room. Check padding, baselines, alignment, readable text and action targets against the project's conventions. A dense list should reduce wasted space without forcing labels into vertical fragments or hiding required actions.

For a new package, discover `project init`. It creates a blank package with no pages (`page draw` makes the first); it does not decide the business requirements, theme dimensions or platform page copies. Configure the first requested design explicitly.

## Adapt the same content

Deliver the agreed first platform, then assess the later platforms against the same business content and capabilities. Do not automatically create Desktop and Mobile copies of every page.

Use the smallest change the requested difference needs:

1. Keep the same page/content structure and use Token combinations for bound value changes: widths, heights, padding, gaps, type and color. Set the values for the chosen project groups. Check the same page with the appropriate explicit combination.
2. Use component variants for local reusable structural differences that values cannot express. A Token combination does not automatically select a component variant.
3. Add a Presentation or separate page only when the overall structure or interaction differs substantially and cannot be expressed through the shared design. Record the reason and preserve shared components and content.

Boolean Tokens can control `visible`; Tokens do not switch layout direction or node trees, and theme selection does not select a component variant. Consult the installed `schema node`, operation schemas and projection diagnostics before relying on layout support. If required behavior exceeds tool support, report the specific gap and resolve the affected design choice using existing requirements where possible; ask only when a user decision is needed. Do not silently duplicate full pages or omit functionality to pass a check. A smaller viewport does not authorize deleting fields, actions or access to full content.

For responsive work, choose the requested small, medium and large review widths from the project's needs. Check the same agreed Presentation with each explicit theme combination. A separate mobile copy passing a check proves nothing about the original Presentation under a small-width theme. Width reduction alone does not adapt a sidebar, long path or action row: decide how each region fits and preserves access. Review density and hierarchy at larger sizes too; avoid excessive empty space or stretched actions. A handful of theme widths is a design sample, not proof of responsive behavior at every width in a production app.

## Inspect and deliver

Use `view` by name, scoped to the Tokens, component, variant, page, platform or element you need. Use `text` to navigate, then **specification** (`--as spec`) for implementation and provenance, **wireframe** for spatial questions, and **PNG** for high-fidelity visual acceptance. These are three views of the shared native layout, not substitutes for each other. Specifications separate authored constraints from actual bounds; preserve fill/hug, inspect field-level Token sources and instance overrides, and read node diagnostics. Expand one `--element` for fonts, colors, borders and declared interactions. A missing rule or measurement is unknown, not an inferred default. Match `layout.hash`, revision, size, themes and state; use `export --format png --evidence` for all three outputs from one solve. `issues` and `validate` report layout, text and contrast checks. `validate` checks every page version or component variant in its selected scope unless one is named; discover its flags rather than assuming it accepts `--all`. Pass explicit `--theme Group/Option` values for each agreed combination; omitting them uses project defaults.

Treat final acceptance as three separate checks:

1. **Data and coverage:** check Token references, binding targets, shared instances, preserved content/actions and prototype links. Run layout/text/contrast checks for the agreed targets and combinations. Read issues, skipped checks and unsupported layout diagnostics. If a whole-package check is too costly, use scoped checks that cover the same targets; count actual page versions and variants, not just report groups. Do not turn an interrupted or partial check into a pass.
2. **Visual review:** inspect the requested pages and relevant component states at a legible scale in each agreed size/theme combination. Look for clipping, bad wrapping, misaligned text/actions, oversized gaps, stretched controls and missing focus borders. Verify that text wraps and its parent grows in the actual renderer; several hugging texts in a row do not share available room automatically, so give the intended flexible text `width: fill` and check the result. Use long content as well as sample labels. Fix defects in the shared component or Token before applying page-specific patches.
3. **App opening:** for a package intended for App review, actually open the final saved package in the App and confirm that the workspace loads and affected pages render. When the user requires CLI authoring, use the App only for permitted inspection. CLI validation and exports do not replace this check. If App access or visual inspection is unavailable or prohibited, continue the checks and repairs you can perform and state the remaining verification explicitly; do not present the package as fully accepted.

Tie every result to the saved package revision, page/Presentation, variant and explicit themes. After a final edit, rerun affected checks and refresh affected exports; retain older report revisions and identify unchanged-scope evidence instead of relabeling them. Record the completed combinations and remaining gaps in `DESIGN.md`. Zero reported issues does not mean complete coverage, visual quality or a working App.

When CLI/App appearance must agree, compare exports with the actual App renderer at the same revision, themes, scale and device pixel ratio. Cover the requested pages and relevant variants. Check that opening and measuring the design leaves its revision unchanged. Record renderer errors, differences and unsupported coverage; do not report pixel identity from data checks alone. SmallPen maintainers can run `npm run test:render-parity` from `smallpen/` after building the frontend to check shared paint/layout semantics in CLI, SVG and WebGL.

People review the design in the SmallPen App and may fix small things there. Keep the latest `revision` any command reports; before writing code or continuing the design, run `changes PACKAGE --since REVISION` to read, by name, what changed (Tokens with old and new values, component variants and elements, page elements, links) and align your code and notes with it.

Connect the requested clickable elements, triggers and destinations. Use explicit prototype steps to verify navigation. Distinguish page transitions from working input, real data saving or a finished application.

Deliver the package path, retained exports if requested, the targets/combinations actually checked and material limits. Fix known opening failures, overflow, clipped required content and broken shared instances before calling the requested design complete. Describe the achieved result and verification; do not promise a perfect design from this Skill or from zero checker issues. Keep one project specification current. Temporary inspection files are not final deliverables. This Skill is independently installable and needs no sibling SmallPen Skill.
